      "snippet": "Yes — and the “best” way to do it is to treat the LLM as a semantic repair proposal engine, not as part of the gate itself.
If SandPipe tries to “auto-fix with an LLM” without a strict protocol, you’ll get silent inventions. The correct pattern is:

SandPipe detects and halts (gate)

LLM proposes a minimal patch (repair)

SandPipe re-validates (gate again)

Only then commit, with a diff and hashes (ledger)

I implemented that protocol as mounted OS artifacts, so it’s not just talk.
